summary: Iowa's only fire tower: 100-ft Aermotor on Yellow River State Forest, rebuilt 1962 (or 1963), NRHP-listed 2021; poor condition, fenced and closed to the public.

facts.design: Aermotor LS40 tower with 7x7 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: Still standing but in poor condition, with the stairs and cab wood rotted. Fenced in and closed to the public, per Wikipedia.

access.note: Fenced in and closed to the public per Wikipedia, which is undated. A 2020 local article says a friends group hoped to make it accessible to the public.

visit.trail_note: Fenced in and closed to the public, per Wikipedia (undated).

events.note: Iowa DNR acquired the tower from the U.S. Forest Service.
Rebuilt on the current site. NHLR and Wikipedia give 1962; Iowa DNR and the 2020 article give 1963 for the build.
Construction year given by Iowa DNR and by a 2020 local article.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2021. Wikidata gives a September 2021 start date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Completion year differs. NHLR and Wikipedia give 1962 for the rebuild on the current site. Iowa DNR and a 2020 local article give 1963 as the build year. The story reports both.

sources.title: Learn about Yellow River State Forest Fire Tower National Historic Register Nomination Project in pair of meeting options this week

notes_for_editor: Wikipedia's statement that the tower is closed to the public is undated, and no current Iowa DNR access statement was found. Re-check before publishing. The NRHP nomination asset page (npgallery) did not load, so the NRHP listing comes from Wikipedia and Wikidata. Listing day differs (Sept 14 vs Sept 17, 2021); the story gives the year only. Wikipedia's infobox names a builder, Bob Menery, which is unverified and not used. Brief status standing is kept with a note on condition. Staffing not found. No photos added.
